title: Attention kernel crossover stability harness and pad-aware scheduling
creator: Devon Patel
description:
Problem: We observe nondeterministic latency and occasional quality regressions when runtime switches between FlashAttention v2 and v3 kernels for mixed sequence-length workloads. Root causes are not limited to numeric differences; scheduling decisions around padded batches, workspace layout, and prefill vs decode kernel handoff also appear to affect cache reuse and tail latency.

Goal: Build a reproducible crossover stability harness that: (1) runs paired side-by-side comparisons of v2 vs v3 across realistic workload distributions (sparsity, padding ratios, batch shapes), (2) surfaces numerical delta statistics and token-level divergence traces, and (3) validates pad-aware scheduling heuristics that prefer fewer kernel switches for padded prefixes. The harness should also automate quantization/precision toggles, microtiling layouts, and workspace reuse permutations so we can triage regressions to scheduling vs kernel math differences.
acceptance_criteria: A harness that can run N=1000 paired requests across configurable distributions and output a CSV with p95 latency, p99, median, and numerical divergence metrics
Integration tests that assert no >1% token-level divergence for non-quantized FP16 runs across v2/v3 on the same model and input set
New pad-aware scheduling policy implemented as an opt-in runtime flag (--pad-aware-prefill) with fallback to existing policy
Benchmark dashboard updated with cross-kernel comparisons and regression alerts for p95/p99 and divergence rates
Documentation and a playbook for triaging a detected crossover regression
tech_notes: Harness will use an injectable kernel selector shim so we can force v2 or v3 for a single request without changing model artifacts
Implement a lightweight trace format: request_id, seed, seq_lengths, pad_ratio, chosen_kernel, workspace_layout, latency_ms, token_diffs (sha256 of token logits diff), and raw divergence count
Use existing microbatcher harness components from ENG-31765 for workload shaping and engineered spike injection
Watch for workspace size rounding differences between v2/v3; add workspace probe that writes pre/post kernel metadata to temp storage for postmortem
We will capture CUDA/SMM counters where possible (L2 hit rate, sm_efficiency) for correlation with latency regressions
rollout_plan: Feature gates: start as runtime flag (--pad-aware-prefill) behind canary toggle in dev cluster
Canary: 2% of production prefill traffic routed to pad-aware policy for a single model family (gpt-compat-7b) for 72h
If stable, expand to 20% and run comparison harness nightly for 7 days, watch for divergence/regression alerts
Fallback: immediate switch to previous scheduling policy on any P0 regression alert (automated rollback in console)
test_plan: Unit tests for kernel selector shim and runtime flag parsing
Synthetic workload tests: systematically vary seq_len distributions (uniform, long-tail, fixed-pad) and measure kernel switch counts + mean workspace reuse
Golden model run: use curated prompt set (internal/gold/pad-aware-set) to assert token-level stability across kernels
Chaos test: induce transient memory pressure and verify scheduling gracefully favors stable kernel to avoid OOMs
Performance CI: p95/p99 sustained under target thresholds on dedicated 80GB A100 hosts
